walkthroughs.body_html:
Environmental & Ecological Economics — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Environmental & Ecological Economics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Environmental & Ecological Economics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why is burning fossil fuels considered to disrupt the carbon cycle?
options: It creates new carbon that did not exist before.
It removes carbon permanently.
It releases carbon stored for millions of years much faster than the cycle can absorb.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: It removes carbon permanently.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
Bacteria produce them.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: 100 percent (everything transfers).
Bacteria produce them.
About 10 percent.
About 50 percent.
